newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate soars on central bank repos.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate soars on central bank repos.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates climbed sharply to close up 210 basis points at 25.50 percent on Wednesday in response to a central bank move to drain liquidity through repurchase agreements rather than auctions, traders said.
"The market did not take well to Banco de Mexico's decision, which put rates under great pressure," a money market analyst said.
Shortly after midday, Banco de Mexico drained 6.423 billion pesos from the system through 10 repurchase agreements settled on the secondary market at rates of between 23.45-26.11 percent.
One analyst suggested the central bank changed its method of draining liquidity because it preferred to use paper at its disposal rather than cash.
"What the central bank needs is liquidity so it is offering its paper for repurchase agreements to obtain that liquidity so the money then does not return to the system," he said.

Other traders said rates had gained in late trade due to a surplus of paper in the system following the liquidity drain, adding that rates had been stable and near to opening levels prior to central bank participation.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile gained 60 basis points to 26.50 percent.
In Cetes futures trading on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, June contracts closed down 40 centavos at 77.40 pesos. Liquidity of 10.108 billion pesos was slated to
return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
